input.quote: (vi) Return of Materials. Within ninety (90) days after the end of the Wind-down Period, upon request by Array, Ono shall either deliver to Array or destroy all tangible items comprising, bearing or containing trademarks of Array (including the Product Trademarks), trade names, patents, copyrights, designs, drawings, formulas or other Data, photographs, samples, literature, sales and promotional aids ("Product Materials") and Confidential Information of Array, that is in Ono's possession, subject to Ono's right to keep one (1) copy for archiving purposes.
input.rationale: Article XIV addresses termination effects but runs in one direction only: Ono must continue Clinical Studies and distribution during the Wind-down Period, assign Regulatory Filings and Marketing Approvals, hand over Data, Ono Know-How and customer data, assign Product Trademarks and domains, and return or destroy Array's Confidential Information and Product Materials (14.2(a)(i)-(viii)). There is no obligation anywhere on Array to (i) provide transition assistance to us, (ii) continue supplying Materials while we remain obliged to distribute Product during the Wind-down Period (Article IX is not listed in the Section 14.5 survival provision), or (iii) return, delete or certify deletion of our Confidential Information and Data. Article X contains no return-or-destroy mechanic either. The "Transition" clause at 14.2(a)(iv) is limited to cooperating in transferring the Product back to Array. No usable clause exists for our side, so the rule's clause is missing rather than at the fallback; we have inserted a reciprocal exit provision at the preferred position (up to six months' assistance at Array's then-current rates, data return within thirty days, certified deletion thereafter), carved back for Array's retained rights under 14.2(a)(iii), (v) and (ix).

proposal.summary: Insert reciprocal Array transition-assistance, continued-supply and return-of-Ono-data obligations in Section 14.2(a)
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article XIV only runs one way: we transfer studies, Regulatory Filings, Data, trademarks and materials to Array, but Array has no obligation to support the transition, to keep supplying Materials while we are required to keep distributing during the Wind-down Period, or to return or destroy our Confidential Information and Data. We have added a reciprocal exit clause (transition assistance for up to six months at Array's then-current rates, return of our data within thirty days and certified destruction thereafter), preserving Array's retained rights under Sections 14.2(a)(iii), (v) and (ix); we can discuss a 90-day assistance period as a fallback.

ops.text: (x) Array Transition Obligations. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Array shall, at Ono's request: (A) continue to supply, or secure supply of, Materials in accordance with Article IX for so long as Ono is required to distribute the Product pursuant to Section 14.2(a)(ii), and provide reasonable transition assistance to Ono for a period of up to six (6) months following the effective date of termination at Array's then-current rates; (B) within thirty (30) days after the later of the effective date of termination and the end of the Wind-down Period, return to Ono all Confidential Information of Ono, and all Data and other materials provided by Ono, in each case in a commonly used, machine-readable format to the extent held in electronic form; and (C) thereafter delete or destroy any remaining copies thereof in its possession and certify such deletion or destruction in writing, in each case subject to Array's rights under Sections 14.2(a)(iii), (v) and (ix) and Array's right to retain one (1) copy for archiving purposes.
